summary: The monitors, alerts and tests that watch the subject are outside the subject's own authority: the subject may not disable, redirect or weaken them, and a task instruction never extends to them. Changes to monitoring need an independent authorization.

modificationAuthority.description: Reference of the account or decision mechanism that may change monitoring; never the monitored subject.

subagentVetoBinding.description: A safety objection raised by a sub-agent cannot be overruled by the orchestrating agent alone.

partialOrder.rule: Not comparable in general; a derived binding MUST keep protectedMonitors and modificationAuthority unchanged and MAY only add alert recipients.

verification.resultMeaning: no change to a protected monitor originated from the subject and every alert reached its recipients
trustAssumptions: the monitoring plane runs where the subject cannot modify it

verification.resultMeaning: a reviewer confirmed that a flagged change was authorized

limitations: A monitor the subject can edit as part of its task is not protected by writing it into a list; the location field of the enforcing channel decides.
